p5baxcn.s: Casual Flatiron sushi spot, the relaxed offshoot of a fancy omakase, open for lunch and dinner with outdoor seating.

pb8p3n.s: SoHo Italian restaurant on West Broadway with a modern take on Italian nostalgia.

p1oeklga.s: Casual Mexican seafood restaurant in Jackson Heights known for excellent aguachile, ceviches, tostadas and massive molcajetes.

p17x6n9u.s: Chinatown fast-food counter on Hester Street, a go-to for Taiwanese fried pork chop over rice.

p1yjnspa.s: Old-school Chinatown bakery on Mott Street, best known for its baked roast pork buns.

p7bzqxg.s: Midtown power-lunch restaurant that Michael McCarty opened in 1989, bringing California's seasonal, local cooking to New York.

pw9rgqw.s: Mikado, a reliable sushi mini-chain with several locations around the city, good for sushi sets and takeout.

pezwq5u.s: Nearly 100-year-old Midtown bar and restaurant, revamped by the 4 Charles Prime Rib team. A fun, nostalgic place for a martini and a burger.

pclq5ab.s: Greenwich Village Italian restaurant open since 1918, full of regulars. Order a Cosmo, and the tartufo for dessert.

p8c9lrw.s: Cathedral-like Koreatown restaurant serving crispy fried chicken and an excellent branzino.

pl2qw4v.s: St. Marks Place location of Szechuan Mountain House, a Michelin-recognized Sichuan restaurant.

p1cmwytq.s: Loft-like Greenpoint restaurant from the team behind Otis: split the bread basket, order fun cocktails and bring friends.

pchtb85.s: East Village branch of Nan Xiang Xiao Long Bao, the popular Flushing soup-dumpling spot. Opened in 2024 as its third NYC location.

pfmclhd.s: Bushwick-born taqueria from Andrés Galindo, the "Birria Taco King of Brooklyn", with some of the city's best birria. Now has several locations.

p1ex143u.s: Two-story Koreatown barbecue on West 32nd Street, one of the few that still cooks over charcoal.

p44m7yi.s: Doyers Street dim sum parlor that opened in 1920, New York's first. Come for the retro diner room and dumplings.

pp3bmgf.s: The East Village original of Nowon, a favorite Korean-American gastropub.

p1gvs9jo.s: José Andrés' luxurious cocktail bar on the 50th floor of the Ritz-Carlton NoMad, with one of the best views in the city.

pm34hb7.s: New York outpost of Seoul chef Ok Dongsik's restaurant, which serves essentially one dish: dwaeji-gomtang, a clear pork-bone soup with rice. It started as a 2022 pop-up.

p1x6ak0r.s: Steakhouse on the Meatpacking-Chelsea border since 1868, older than almost every steakhouse in New York, with time-capsule decor.

ps5tqhx.s: Rice-ball counter inside Katagiri, New York's oldest Japanese grocer, on Lexington Avenue.

ppa6b13.s: Michelin-starred Greenpoint restaurant cooking creative Mexican food over wood fire, plus classic cocktails.

p1nek4v1.s: East Village Indian restaurant on 1st Avenue known for a ceiling covered in lights.

p1d2m4wj.s: Legendary Greenpoint pizzeria that opened in 2010. It closed in April 2026 and reopened as Me And Paul's.

p1a5vikl.s: Bed-Stuy Southern spot, open for nearly two decades and famous for Nashville-style hot chicken.

p1mtz98l.s: Williamsburg's 130-plus-year-old steakhouse, the classic place for a sizzling porterhouse.

phmsant.s: SoHo outpost of Rome's famous Roscioli: expert carbonara and burrata blanketed in anchovies.

p8mywfh.s: Hell's Kitchen dive on 9th Avenue since 1933, famous for cheap beer and free hot dogs.

pnr6jyc.s: Fourth-generation appetizing shop on East Houston since 1914, famous for bagels and lox, smoked fish, caviar, herring and babka.

p1o708zt.s: Full-service restaurant from the Russ & Daughters family on Orchard Street, serving Jewish comfort food and the shop's famous fish.

pq9r1nn.s: Sceney Koreatown dinner and drinks spot modeled on a Korean sool-jib (drinking house), recognized by the Michelin Guide.

p1b8ogk0.s: Buzzing, cash-only pho and bánh mì spot on MacDougal Street, popular with NYU students.

pr39598.s: Little Italy institution for cheap, excellent bánh mì, with a second location in Sunset Park.

p1eunm20.s: Elmhurst Thai restaurant making notably herby, fragrant dishes.

pv90y2g.s: Chef Scott Conant's Italian restaurant, known for its pastas, including the famous spaghetti and duck-and-foie gras ravioli.

p5re9hk.s: West Village South Indian restaurant from the Unapologetic Foods team, with bold regional cooking. A guaranteed date-night win.

potmi9f.s: Hidden Koreatown sushi counter modeled on Tokyo's standing bars: in and out in 30 minutes for under $50.

p1puema0.s: Flushing favorite for some of the city's best xiao long bao, including a giant soup dumpling served with a straw.

p1evh7to.s: Cheap, beloved Fuzhou-style spot on Grand Street for pork-and-chive dumplings and peanut-sauce noodles.

pnuciny.s: Cash-only, BYOB Sri Lankan restaurant upstairs on 1st Avenue in the East Village.

p1srtvuu.s: Classic New York steakhouse that opened in 1977, serving USDA Prime dry-aged steaks in a raucous room.

pajsv6.s: Lower East Side counter making Sonoran-style burritos with soft, chewy flour tortillas, and never any rice.
